title: Context Activity Buckets — Parent, Grouping, Category, Other
description: Interactive Mermaid MicroSim showing how a single xAPI statement's main object relates to multiple activities through the four context activity buckets: parent, grouping, category, and other.
creator: xAPI for Intelligent Textbooks
subject: xAPI / Learning Analytics
chapter_title: Advanced Statement Structure — Voiding, Sub-Statements, Extensions, and Attachments
learning_objective: Identify the role of each context activity bucket and explain how a single statement's main object can be related to multiple activities through different bucket relationships.

learningObjectives: Identify the four context activity buckets by name and recall the relationship each expresses (directly contains, is a member of, conforms to, associated with).
Distinguish Parent (structural container) from Grouping (set membership), and explain why a single activity has only one parent but can have many groupings.
Recognize that the category bucket is how a statement declares conformance to an xAPI profile, and that profiles like CMI5 require it.
Decide when to use the other bucket vs. a custom extension for recording relationships that don't fit the first three.
prerequisites: Familiarity with the xAPI statement triple (Actor, Verb, Object)
Working mental model of an IRI

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Click-to-reveal definition with concrete shared example
keyQuestions: What does it mean for an activity to be the 'main object' of a statement vs. sitting in contextActivities?
Why can the same activity be in only one parent but in many groupings?
How does the category bucket relate to xAPI profiles like CMI5?
When should you reach for the other bucket vs. a custom extension?
commonMisconceptions: Treating Parent and Grouping as interchangeable.
Forgetting that category is required by some profiles (CMI5).
Using the other bucket for data that should be a typed extension.
assessmentOpportunities: Given a JSON contextActivities block, name each entry's bucket and the relationship it expresses.
Given an activity from the learner's domain, propose values for all four buckets.
Identify which bucket is missing in a statement that fails CMI5 conformance.
